root_motivation: Grounding (PRD; visions/mcphost-end-user-auth.md wwhtbt leaf 1; 2026-09-23 client research and 'OAuth broken on 119/119 servers', wiki 2026-09-23-mcphost-discovery-icp-use-cases-pmf): two of six client families in the client research (Claude.ai connectors, ChatGPT developer mode) connect only through the MCP authorization spec (OAuth 2.1 with protected-resource metadata); mcphost answered neither the metadata route nor the 401 challenge (scout: routes in http.rs:522-553 were healthz, catalog, billing, hooks, exports, claim -- none of them this). A working implementation is a visible differentiator for the SaaS-PM ICP precisely because it is broken everywhere else; today an agent operator on an OAuth-only client cannot connect at all.
user_persona: Four (PRD User stories): (1) the agent operator on an OAuth-capable client, who needs the client to discover resource metadata and complete its issuer's login with no key in the transcript; (2) the tenant owner, who calls host.oauth.issuer_set once so tokens from that issuer act as their tenant; (3) the operator, who needs admin.oauth.issuers to see registered issuers, JWKS age, and rejection counts; (4) the key-based agent, for whom nothing changes.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given no issuers registered, When GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource is called, Then it returns 200 JSON with resource equal to the public URL and authorization_servers: [].

Given a tenant registered issuer I with audience A and a JWKS URL served by a test server, When a JWT signed by that JWKS with iss=I, aud=A, exp in the future calls host.state.get, Then the call runs as that tenant and subject equals the JWT sub.

Given the same setup, When a JWT with a wrong signature, an expired exp, or aud!=A is presented, Then each returns 401 invalid_token with the matching error_description and the rejection counter for that reason increments.

Given a tool that requires a tenant, When it is called with neither key nor bearer over streamable HTTP, Then the response is 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header naming the metadata URL; signup without credentials still succeeds.
Given an unknown kid, When a token arrives, Then the JWKS is refetched once, and a second unknown kid within 60s is rejected without a refetch.
Given the JWKS server is down, When a token arrives for an issuer with no cached JWKS, Then the token is rejected with unknown_issuer and the host stays healthy.
Given tenant T1 registered issuer I, When tenant T2 calls host.oauth.issuer_set with the same issuer, Then it is rejected as already registered; T1 may register up to 3 and the 4th is rejected.
Given a request with both a valid key for T1 and a valid bearer for T2, When it runs, Then it is rejected with conflicting_credentials.
Given two issuers, When admin.oauth.issuers runs, Then both appear with tenant id, JWKS age, and per-reason rejection counters, and admin_audit records the call.
Given the existing key-based test suites, When they run against this build, Then they pass unchanged.

Given prod after land, When a Claude.ai connector is pointed at https://mcphost.dev with a test issuer registered by the operator tenant, Then the connector completes the flow and host.state.get succeeds through it (Live).
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned; needs a real Claude.ai connector run against production https://mcphost.dev with operator-held issuer credentials and network egress this coding sandbox does not have. See the coder dispatch's own deferred list and PRD Acceptance criteria 11 (evidence: mcphost-1 healthz version after deploy plus the call transcript, saved under docs/receipts/<slug>.md).

scope: migrations/0037_oauth_issuers.sql (new; PRD said 0038, actual next-free number was 0037 -- last existing was 0036_ban_removed_at.sql): oauth_issuers table (tenant_id/issuer/audience/jwks_url/created_at/last_jwks_at/jwks_json) and oauth_rejections (issuer, reason, count) for AC3/AC5's per-reason counters.

src/oauth.rs (new): JwksCache (refetch-on-unknown-kid throttled to once per 60s per issuer, staleness via MCPHOST_OAUTH_JWKS_TTL_SECS), validate_bearer (the full decode/issuer-lookup/signature/aud/exp/nbf/sub pipeline), issuer_set/issuer_remove/issuers_list (tenant tools), admin_issuers/admin_jwks_refresh (admin tools), protected_resource_metadata (RFC 9728 document).

src/errors.rs: new AppError variants IssuerAlreadyRegistered, IssuerQuotaExceeded, IssuerNotFound, InvalidToken(reason), ConflictingCredentials, each with code()/jsonrpc_code()/into_error_data() wiring (InvalidToken carries error_description, matching RFC 6750's bearer-error vocabulary).

src/handler.rs: Auth::Tenant grows a second field (Option<String>, the OAuth sub claim, None for key-based); resolve_auth's key-hash-miss path checks for a 3-segment (JWT-shaped) credential and calls oauth::validate_bearer instead of failing closed; AC8's conflicting-credentials check runs when both a tenant_key argument and a bearer resolve to different tenants; dispatch_tenant_tool/dispatch_admin_tool gain the 5 new host.oauth.*/admin.oauth.* tool arms.

src/http.rs: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (AC1); an oauth_401_upgrade middleware layered over the whole router that inspects a JSON-RPC error response's error.data.error_code and, for tenant_key_missing/invalid_token, rewrites the HTTP status to 401 and adds WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=... (AC4) -- chosen over per-route middleware since call_tool's JSON-RPC errors don't otherwise carry a real HTTP status, and tower is not already a dependency of this crate.
src/control.rs: whoami(tenant, subject) exposes the OAuth subject (None for key-based) so AC2 can assert on it.
src/admin.rs: admin.oauth.issuers/jwks_refresh audit rows (admin.oauth.issuers is a deliberate exception to the 'read-only admin.* listings aren't audited' convention -- AC9 requires it).
Cargo.toml: jsonwebtoken = "9" (new direct dependency; PRD Technical considerations named it as the crate to reuse if present, and it was not).
non_goals: Running an authorization server (login pages, consent, token issuance) -- PRD Non-goals; bring-your-own issuer only.
Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) on mcphost's side -- PRD Non-goals.
Per-end-user semantics -- PRD Non-goals; this PRD only validates and exposes caller.subject, the identity PRD reads it.

MCPHOST_OAUTH_ALLOWED_ALGS/MCPHOST_OAUTH_JWKS_TTL_SECS env overrides beyond parsing+defaults (P2 requirement 8) -- implemented since they were low-cost and shared code paths with the P0 defaults, but no AC exercises non-default values.

additional.no_token_content_ever_logged: PRD requirement 5: rejection counters are per-reason-per-issuer only (oauth_rejections(issuer, reason, count)); no code path logs a raw JWT or its decoded claims.
additional.jwks_fetch_failure_degrades_to_rejection: PRD Non-functional: fetch_jwks returns None on any timeout/non-2xx/parse failure, and every KeyResolution arm that can't produce a verified key rejects with invalid_token (unknown_issuer/bad_signature) rather than skipping verification.
additional.metadata_document_lists_issuer_urls_only: PRD Technical considerations: protected_resource_metadata's authorization_servers is list_distinct_oauth_issuer_urls() -- issuer URLs only, no tenant id/namespace, since the document is public and unauthenticated.
additional.bearer_path_joins_the_existing_key_path_: PRD Technical considerations ('auth.rs resolves the caller once per request'): this crate's equivalent is resolve_auth in handler.rs (no separate auth.rs existed); the bearer branch was added inside that same function rather than as a parallel code path, so every downstream match on Auth sees one enum.
additional.challenge_header_before_mcp_json_parsing: PRD Technical considerations: oauth_401_upgrade is layered as router-wide middleware (via Router::layer), which runs before the streamable-HTTP handler's own JSON-RPC parsing/dispatch.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build OAuth resource-server support now, rather than leaving the pasted-key argument as the only auth path?
five_whys_trace.a: The 2026-09-23 client research found two of six client families (Claude.ai connectors, ChatGPT developer mode) connect only through the MCP authorization spec, and OAuth is broken on 119 of 119 public MCP servers surveyed -- a working implementation is a visible differentiator for the SaaS-PM ICP, and today those client shapes cannot connect at all (tenants of that shape number zero).

five_whys_trace.q: Why bring-your-own-issuer rather than mcphost running its own authorization server?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD Non-goals/Open questions: hosting login pages, consent, and token issuance is a separate, larger decision (open question, owned by Joe, due after the first OAuth tenant) -- bring-your-own-issuer gets the connect-at-all outcome without that scope.

five_whys_trace.q: Why cache the JWKS (with a throttled refetch-on-unknown-kid) rather than fetching per request?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD Non-functional: bearer validation must add < 1ms with a warm JWKS; a network round trip to the issuer's JWKS endpoint on every authenticated call would add real, variable latency to the hot path every host.*/billing.* call already goes through.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an unknown kid refetch at most once per 60s per issuer, rather than on every unknown-kid token?
five_whys_trace.a: AC5 names this directly: an attacker (or a misconfigured client) sending a stream of tokens with bogus kids would otherwise turn every rejected call into an outbound JWKS fetch -- a cheap denial-of-service surface against the host's own egress and the issuer's JWKS endpoint.

five_whys_trace.q: Why reject on conflicting key+bearer credentials rather than picking one (e.g. bearer wins)?
five_whys_trace.a: AC8/requirement 7: silently preferring one credential over a disagreeing other is a silent cross-tenant confusion risk (a caller could probe which of two tenants a mixed request resolves to); refusing outright makes the ambiguity visible to the caller instead of resolved by an implicit precedence rule.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD requirement 3 names migration '0038' for oauth_issuers, but the repo's last existing migration is 0036_ban_removed_at.sql -- use the PRD's literal number or the actual next-free one?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Used 0037 (the actual next-free number). The PRD's own migration numbers are indicative, not authoritative over the repo's real sequence; a gap at 0037 would leave an unexplained hole, and no AC or other file references '0038' literally.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The PRD's Engineering target line names auth.rs as the file the bearer path joins the key path in, but this repo has no auth.rs -- where does caller resolution actually live?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: handler.rs's resolve_auth is this crate's equivalent (the PRD's own Technical considerations describes the property -- 'one Caller type with tenant_id and subject' -- not a literal path); the bearer branch was added inside that same function per the same one-resolver principle.

ambiguities_resolved.question: AC7's '4th is rejected' and requirement 3's 'up to 3 issuers' don't state the rejection's error shape -- reuse an existing error or add a new one?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Added AppError::IssuerQuotaExceeded{limit, used} (new variant, code issuer_quota_exceeded) rather than reusing a generic validation error, matching this crate's existing convention of one AppError variant per distinct caller-facing rejection reason (e.g. IssuerAlreadyRegistered is the separate, adjacent case for AC7's 'same issuer, different tenant' half).
